rv.q: For once the so-called theatrical event of the year really is just that
It's a triumph...In all key respects, it grips, it stirs, it delights…You can't stop watching.
Forget that yawny Lord of the Rings musical: Potter looks set to be the one West End play to rule them all, to find them, to bring them all in.
Tiffany and his team stage the piece with such dazzling assurance that I finally began to see the point of being wild about Harry.
The result, delivered in two parts, is thrilling: gripping, dark, wittily acted and often visually dazzling.

For any Potterhead who can get their hands on a ticket, it will no doubt be a fantastic experience; for those not already enamoured by Rowling’s wizarding, The Cursed Child is still captivating, but may be a slightly long ride.
But this is far more than just a show for the fans – it’s a truly game-changing production and a thrilling theatrical endeavour in its own right.

‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’ is an absolute hoot, a joyous, big-hearted, ludicrously incident-packed and magic-heavy romp that has to stand as one of the most unrelentingly entertaining things to hit the West End.
This story is meant to be witnessed on stage.
Gripping, poignant and, at times, chilling – put it on your ‘must watch
